scenes.title: Turn your idea into a buildable agreement
scenes.intro: The capstone tests how you lead the process, not how quickly you ship an app.

items.label: Choose the idea
items.detail: Use your own small idea or the fictional tracker.
items.anchor: Choose a small idea you care about

items.label: Keep the goal bounded
items.detail: A polished app in one sitting is not the target.
items.anchor: not to produce a polished app

items.label: Lead the process
items.detail: Reach a bounded, testable plan from an unstructured idea.
items.anchor: lead the process from an unstructured idea

items.label: Explain verification
items.detail: Say how execution would be checked.
items.anchor: explain how execution would be verified

items.label: Use synthetic examples
items.detail: Keep real messages and outside systems out of the exercise.
items.anchor: Use synthetic examples

conclusion.text: The exercise builds a plan without creating real external effects.

scenes.title: Capture the idea, then agree on the journey
scenes.intro: A structured readback turns your raw context into observable behavior.

items.label: Owner · brain dump
items.detail: Problem, people, experience, constraints, uncertainty.
items.anchor: Write a brief brain dump

items.label: Agent · mirror
items.detail: Return a structured readback for correction.
items.anchor: Ask an agent for a structured readback

items.label: Owner · journey
items.detail: Name actor, trigger, actions, and result.
items.anchor: Your final journey must name an actor

items.label: Shared record
items.detail: Separate agreement from what remains unknown.
items.anchor: Record what you agreed

items.label: Stay on behavior
items.detail: Bring premature technology choices back to the readback.
items.anchor: If the agent proposes technology

conclusion.text: When the behavior is already agreed, continue from that point.
conclusion.anchor: If the behavior is already agreed

scenes.title: Research reality and preserve decisions
scenes.intro: Your package should distinguish evidence, plans, and uncertainty.

items.label: Reality scan
items.detail: What exists, what is verified, what is only planned.
items.anchor: Create a small reality scan

items.label: Evidence
items.detail: Cite the actual observations you have.
items.anchor: Cite actual evidence where available

items.label: Decision ledger
items.detail: Two material choices with reasons and reopen conditions.
items.anchor: List two material decisions

items.label: Tracker example
items.detail: Existing form first; email import deferred.
items.anchor: support the existing form first

conclusion.text: A diagram or simulated response does not prove a real integration is live.
conclusion.anchor: based only on a planned diagram

scenes.title: Map the system, then specify behavior
scenes.intro: Trace success and failure before turning the design into a contract.

items.label: Component diagram
items.detail: Each component has a responsibility.
items.anchor: Draw a component diagram

items.label: Two workflows
items.detail: Trace one success and one failure.
items.anchor: trace one successful and one failed workflow

items.label: Boundaries
items.detail: Source of truth, access boundary, and recovery concern.
items.anchor: Identify the source of truth

items.label: Build specification
items.detail: Inputs, outputs, errors, preservation, checks, rollback.
items.anchor: Write a build specification

items.label: Observable behavior
items.detail: Translate broad claims into things you can check.
items.anchor: Translate broad claims into observable behaviors

conclusion.text: If automatic email is forbidden, preserve that boundary in the spec.
conclusion.anchor: the spec must preserve that boundary

callouts.text: Specify failures, preservation requirements, acceptance checks, and rollback.
callouts.anchor: state changes, errors, security, preservation requirements

scenes.title: Prepare the kickoff and the long-run limits
scenes.intro: Organize work before handing it to an execution agent.

items.label: Ordered phases
items.detail: Break the work into an intentional sequence.
items.anchor: Break the work into ordered phases

items.label: Parallel ownership
items.detail: Define shared interfaces and exclusive file ownership.
items.anchor: Give parallel work exclusive ownership

items.label: KICKOFF.md
items.detail: Location, baseline, reading, decisions, checks, handoff.
items.anchor: Write a kickoff with the project location

items.label: Unavailable capability
items.detail: Explain how to proceed with no model or usage visibility.
items.anchor: Explain how the agent should proceed

items.label: Long-run boundaries
items.detail: Include a checkpoint and stop conditions.
items.anchor: Include a checkpoint and stop conditions

conclusion.text: A plan does not itself authorize deployment or unrelated external changes.
conclusion.anchor: Planning does not by itself authorize deployment

callouts.text: The kickoff carries the baseline, authority, and settled decisions forward.

scenes.title: Let a cold reader challenge the package
scenes.intro: The reader should not need to reconstruct the original conversation.

items.label: Fresh reader
items.detail: Which documents govern this behavior?
items.anchor: Can they tell which documents govern a behavior

items.label: Fresh reader
items.detail: What is the first safe action?
items.anchor: Can they identify the first safe action

items.label: Fresh reader
items.detail: What evidence supports each important claim?
items.anchor: Is each important claim paired with appropriate evidence

items.label: Fresh reader
items.detail: What stays unchanged, and how do failures recover?
items.anchor: Does the plan say what stays unchanged

items.label: Revision
items.detail: Use the rubric and repair places where the reader guesses.
items.anchor: the package where a fresh reader must guess

conclusion.text: A successful package is clear, bounded, testable, and restartable.

scenes.title: Choose a scope you can actually explain
scenes.intro: A small project gives the workflow enough substance without unnecessary breadth.

items.label: A few sentences
items.detail: Keep the project small enough to describe clearly.
items.anchor: Pick a project small enough to describe

items.label: Tracker ingredients
items.detail: Public input, private owner, one record, failure cases.
items.anchor: it has a public input

items.label: Your own idea
items.detail: Name the real outcome and exclude a tempting future feature.
items.anchor: If you choose your own idea

items.label: Agent collaboration
items.detail: Work with an agent throughout the exercise.
items.anchor: You can work with an agent

conclusion.text: Preserve your intentions in an actionable, testable starting package.

scenes.title: Assess the mirror, not the agent’s confidence
scenes.intro: The agreed statement should preserve your intent and reveal suggestions.

items.label: Owner
items.detail: Give the raw idea and request a structured mirror.
items.anchor: Give your raw idea to the agent

items.label: Compare
items.detail: Check people, trigger, actions, and final state.
items.anchor: Check the people involved

items.label: Correct
items.detail: Fix an assumption or ambiguity.
items.anchor: Correct an assumption or ambiguity

items.label: Record
items.detail: Save agreement and unresolved questions.
items.anchor: Record the final agreed statement

items.label: Provenance
items.detail: Separate what you said from what the agent suggested.
items.anchor: distinguish what you actually said

conclusion.text: Include the source of settled decisions instead of reopening them.
conclusion.anchor: include its source rather than forcing

scenes.title: Trace the diagram with your finger
scenes.intro: A simple diagram should make responsibilities and recovery visible.

items.label: Responsibilities
items.detail: Each component needs a clear job.
items.anchor: Does each component have a clear job

items.label: Successful request
items.detail: Trace the request from beginning to end.
items.anchor: Can you trace a valid request

items.label: Record + input
items.detail: Locate the authoritative record and untrusted input.
items.anchor: What is the authoritative record

items.label: Private access
items.detail: Identify who may view or change private data.
items.anchor: Who may view or change private data

items.label: Failure branch
items.detail: Trace a storage outage and its recovery.
items.anchor: Now trace a failure

conclusion.text: Label any unverified facts the diagram depends on as assumptions.

scenes.title: Ask how three requirements will be proven
scenes.intro: Acceptance criteria should resolve differing interpretations.

items.label: Fresh-reader proof
items.detail: Choose three requirements and ask how to verify them.
items.anchor: Choose three requirements

items.label: Acceptance criteria
items.detail: Add clarity wherever the answers differ.
items.anchor: Add acceptance criteria where answers differ

items.label: Representative cases
items.detail: Success, invalid input, failure or unauthorized access.
items.anchor: Include a success path

items.label: Preservation + recovery
items.detail: Name what stays intact, work order, and proposed rollback.
items.anchor: List what the build must preserve

conclusion.text: State provider or permission dependencies instead of assuming access.

scenes.title: Make the next safe action obvious
scenes.intro: The final kickoff and handoff must work for a reader who starts cold.

items.label: Locate authority
items.detail: Point to governing documents and the baseline.
items.anchor: find the governing documents

items.label: Act within permission
items.detail: Name allowed work and the first safe action.
items.anchor: know what is allowed

items.label: Find gaps
items.detail: Ask the reader for contradictions or missing dependencies.
items.anchor: Ask the fresh reader to identify any contradiction

items.label: Label the evidence
items.detail: Built, offline-tested, accepted, observed, and pending differ.
items.anchor: A useful handoff also distinguishes built

items.label: Plan-only outcome
items.detail: If this capstone is a plan, say so.
items.anchor: If your capstone is only a plan

conclusion.text: A clearly labeled plan is a valid outcome for this exercise.
conclusion.anchor: That is a valid outcome for this exercise

scenes.title: Use review to improve the package
scenes.intro: Keep the useful lessons while distinguishing simulation from observation.

items.label: Score + note guesses
items.detail: Record where the reader had to guess.
items.anchor: Score each rubric item

items.label: Revise + explain again
items.detail: Ask the reader to explain the revised section.
items.anchor: Revise your package

items.label: Simulated review
items.detail: An agent can find confusing language.
items.anchor: A simulated agent review can find confusing language

items.label: Real beginner
items.detail: A simulation is not a real learner observation.
items.anchor: not the same as observing a real beginner

items.label: Carry learning forward
items.detail: Save better prompts, clearer templates, and failure patterns.
items.anchor: Keep the useful lessons for your next project

conclusion.text: The package becomes a foundation for authorizing a safe build.
conclusion.anchor: a foundation for authorizing a safe build

scenes.title: Leave the understanding with the work
scenes.intro: A transfer note preserves the decisions and identifies what must be rechecked.

items.label: Stable decisions
items.detail: Which choices should remain stable?
items.anchor: Which decisions should remain stable

items.label: Environment assumptions
items.detail: Which assumptions belong to the current environment?
items.anchor: Which assumptions are tied to the current environment

items.label: Fresh confirmation
items.detail: Which costs or permissions need another check?
items.anchor: Which costs or permissions need fresh confirmation

items.label: Transfer note
items.detail: Answer the questions and point to the artifacts.
items.anchor: Write a short note that answers these questions

conclusion.text: Understanding, decisions, evidence, and next actions outlive the original chat.
conclusion.anchor: the original conversation is no longer in context

callouts.text: Keep the understanding and evidence available to the next team.
callouts.anchor: understanding, decisions, evidence, and the next action
